chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, Ṣafwān, and more than one person, they raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

If the married adulterer confesses, the Imam is the first to stone him, then the people. And if the evidence is established against him, the witnesses are the first to stone him, then the Imam, then the people.

key_terms.الزَّانِي الْمُحْصَنُ: a married adulterer subject to the legal ruling of rajm
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the lawful authority who leads implementation of the legal punishment
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legally established proof, here referring to witness testimony
key_terms.يَرْجُمُهُ: stones him as the prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: Who begins the stoning punishment in a zina case when it is proven by confession or by witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the order of carrying out rajm in the case of a muhsan adulterer. It distinguishes between a confession and proof established by bayyinah, assigning precedence in implementation accordingly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5009 - Narrated by Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, Safwan, and others, who reported it to Abu Abdullah (as), that Imam (as) said:

"If a married adulterer confesses, the Imam should be the first to stone him, followed by the people. But if the evidence is established against him, the witnesses should be the first to stone him, then the Imam, and then the people."
